cat.text: A cat is a mammal, like a dog or a cow.
A baby cat is called a kitten.

hat.text: You wear a hat on your head.
A sun hat keeps the sun off your face.

bat.text: A bat is a mammal that can fly.
A bat can also be a stick for hitting a ball.

rat.text: A rat is a small animal with a long tail.
A rat is bigger than a mouse.

mat.text: Wipe your feet on the mat by the door.
A mat is a flat rug that lies on the floor.

map.text: A map shows you where places are.
A map of the world shows land and sea.

cap.text: A cap is a hat with a brim in front.
A pen cap covers the tip of a pen.

nap.text: A nap is a short sleep in the day.
Babies and cats take lots of naps.

bag.text: You carry things in a bag.
A bag can be made of paper, cloth, or plastic.

tag.text: A tag on a shirt tells its size.
In the game of tag, you run and try to touch someone.

jam.text: Jam is made from fruit and sugar.

ham.text: Ham is meat that comes from a pig.
You can put ham in a sandwich.

van.text: A van is a vehicle, like a car or a bus.
A van can carry lots of boxes.

fan.text: A fan blows air to keep you cool.
A fan is also someone who loves a team.

pan.text: You cook food in a pan on the stove.
A pan is made of metal, so it gets hot.

man.text: A boy grows up to be a man.
A man and a woman are both grown-ups.

dad.text: Your dad's mom is your grandma.
Dad is another word for father.

sad.text: Sad is the opposite of happy.
You might feel sad when you lose a toy.

lap.text: Your lap is the top of your legs when you sit.
A lap is also once around a track.

wag.text: A dog wags its tail when it is happy.
To wag means to move from side to side.

pig.text: A pig is a farm animal, like a cow or a sheep.
A baby pig is called a piglet.

big.text: Big is the opposite of small.
An elephant is bigger than a dog.

dig.text: You dig a hole with a shovel.
Moles and rabbits dig holes under the ground.

wig.text: A wig is hair you can put on and take off.

sit.text: Sit is the opposite of stand.

fin.text: A fish uses its fins to swim.
A shark has a fin on its back.

pin.text: A pin is sharp, so be careful.

lip.text: You have a top lip and a bottom lip.
Your lips help you talk and smile.

zip.text: You zip your coat to close it.
A zipper has two rows of little teeth.

kid.text: A baby goat is also called a kid.

dog.text: A dog is a mammal, like a cat or a horse.
A baby dog is called a puppy.

log.text: A log is a big piece of a tree.
You can burn logs in a fire.

hop.text: To hop, you jump on one foot.

top.text: Top is the opposite of bottom.
A top is also a toy that spins.

pot.text: You cook soup in a pot.
A plant can grow in a pot of dirt.

hot.text: Hot is the opposite of cold.
Fire and the sun are hot.

fox.text: A fox is a wild animal, like a wolf.
A fox has a long, bushy tail.

box.text: You can keep toys in a box.
A box has corners and flat sides.

mop.text: You clean the floor with a mop.
A mop and a broom are both for cleaning.

rod.text: A fishing rod helps you catch fish.
A rod is a long, thin stick.

sun.text: The sun gives us light and heat.

run.text: You run faster than you walk.
Horses and cheetahs run very fast.

bun.text: A bun is a small, round bread.
A hot dog goes in a bun.

bug.text: Ants, bees, and beetles are all bugs.

hug.text: You hug someone with your arms.
A hug can show someone you love them.

mug.text: A mug is a cup with a handle.
You drink hot cocoa from a mug.

cup.text: A cup can hold milk, juice, or water.

pup.text: A pup is a baby dog.
Baby seals are called pups too.

bus.text: A bus is a vehicle, like a car or a train.

tub.text: You take a bath in a tub.
A tub is a big container that holds water.

nut.text: An acorn is a nut from an oak tree.

bed.text: You sleep in a bed at night.
A bed has a pillow and a blanket.

red.text: Red is a color, like blue and green.
Apples, strawberries, and fire trucks can be red.

pen.text: A pen is also a fence that keeps pigs in.

hen.text: A hen is a girl chicken.

ten.text: Ten is one more than nine.

net.text: You catch fish with a net.
A net is full of little holes.

wet.text: Wet is the opposite of dry.

web.text: A spider spins a web to catch bugs.
A spider's web is made of silk.

leg.text: A dog has four legs, and a bird has two.

ship.text: A ship is a big boat.

shop.text: You buy things at a shop.
A bakery is a shop that sells bread.

fish.text: A fish lives in water and breathes with gills.
Sharks and goldfish are both fish.

dish.text: You eat food from a dish.
Plates and bowls are both dishes.

wish.text: You make a wish when you blow out candles.
A wish is something you hope will happen.

chin.text: Your chin is below your mouth.
You can rest your chin on your hand.

chip.text: A chip is a thin, crunchy snack.
A potato chip is made from a potato.

chop.text: You chop wood with an axe.
To chop means to cut into pieces.

rich.text: Rich means having lots of money.
Rich is the opposite of poor.

thin.text: Thin is the opposite of thick.
A pencil is thin, but a tree trunk is thick.

moth.text: A moth is an insect, like a butterfly.

bath.text: You get clean in a bath.
A bath uses soap and warm water.

duck.text: A duck is a bird that can swim.
A baby duck is called a duckling.

sock.text: You wear socks on your feet.
Socks come in pairs, one for each foot.

rock.text: A pebble is a small, smooth rock.

kick.text: You kick a ball with your foot.
Soccer players kick the ball into the goal.

bell.text: A bell makes a ringing sound.
A bike bell tells people you are coming.

doll.text: A doll is a toy that looks like a person.
You can dress a doll in tiny clothes.

hill.text: A hill is smaller than a mountain.
You can sled down a snowy hill.

kiss.text: You kiss someone with your lips.
A kiss can say I love you.

frog.text: A frog can live in water and on land.
A tadpole grows up to be a frog.

stop.text: Stop is the opposite of go.

flag.text: Every country has its own flag.
A flag waves in the wind.

crab.text: A crab walks sideways on the sand.
A crab has a hard shell and two claws.

drum.text: You hit a drum to make music.
A drum is an instrument, like a piano or a flute.

clap.text: You clap your hands to make a sound.
People clap when they like a show.

plum.text: A plum is a fruit, like a peach or a cherry.
A dried plum is called a prune.

swim.text: Ducks can swim, and most can fly too.

sled.text: You ride a sled down a snowy hill.

snap.text: You snap your fingers to make a click.
A twig snaps when you break it.

spot.text: A leopard has spots, but a tiger has stripes.

trip.text: A trip is when you travel somewhere.
You can take a trip by car, train, or plane.

jump.text: Kangaroos jump with their strong back legs.
You jump up and land on your feet.

hand.text: You have five fingers on each hand.
You use your hands to hold things.

nest.text: A bird's nest holds its eggs.
Many birds build nests out of twigs and grass.

milk.text: Cheese and butter are made from milk.

tent.text: You sleep in a tent when you go camping.
A tent is made of cloth held up by poles.

lamp.text: A lamp gives light when it is dark.
A lamp can light up a dark room.

belt.text: You wear a belt around your waist.
A belt helps hold your pants up.

gift.text: A gift is something you give to someone.

cake.text: You eat cake on your birthday.
A cake is made from flour, eggs, and sugar.

lake.text: A lake is water with land all around it.
A lake is bigger than a pond.

game.text: In a game, you follow the rules.

gate.text: A gate is a door in a fence.
You open the gate to go in.

bike.text: You pedal a bike to make it go.

kite.text: A kite flies high in the wind.
You hold a kite by its long string.

time.text: A clock tells you the time.
Morning, noon, and night are times of day.

ride.text: You can ride a horse or a bike.
To ride means to sit on something that moves.

five.text: Five is one more than four.
You have five fingers on one hand.

home.text: Your home is where you live.
A shell is a snail's home.

rope.text: A rope is made of strings twisted together.
You pull a rope in tug of war.

nose.text: An elephant's nose is called a trunk.

cube.text: A cube has six square faces.

tube.text: A tube is long, round, and hollow.

cute.text: Cute means sweet and nice to look at.

mule.text: A mule is part horse and part donkey.
Mules carry heavy loads up mountains.

hope.text: To hope is to wish something will happen.
I hope it is sunny tomorrow.

lime.text: A lime is a green fruit.
A lime is sour, like a lemon.

wave.text: You wave your hand to say hi.
A wave is water moving in the sea.

tail.text: A fish swims with its tail.

snail.text: A snail carries its shell on its back.

feet.text: You wear shoes on your feet.

bee.text: A bee has six legs and four wings.

tree.text: A tree is a plant with a trunk.

seed.text: A plant grows from a seed.

sheep.text: A baby sheep is called a lamb.

boat.text: A boat is a vehicle, like a car or a plane.

goat.text: A goat can climb steep rocks.
Goats give milk, just like cows.

road.text: A road goes from one place to another.

soap.text: You wash your hands with soap.

car.text: A car is a vehicle, like a bus or a truck.

star.text: Stars shine in the sky at night.
Stars look tiny because they are far away.

park.text: You play on the swings at the park.
To park a car means to stop it and leave it.

farm.text: Cows, pigs, and sheep live on a farm.
A farmer grows food on a farm.

fork.text: A fork, a spoon, and a knife are all for eating.

horn.text: A rhino has a horn on its nose.

storm.text: Thunder and lightning come with some storms.

tall.text: A giraffe is tall, so it can eat leaves high up.
Tall is the opposite of short.

short.text: Short is the opposite of tall.
A pencil gets shorter when you sharpen it.

long.text: A snake has a long body.
Long is the opposite of short.

wide.text: A river is wide, so you need a bridge to cross it.
Wide is the opposite of narrow.

deep.text: Deep is the opposite of shallow.

flat.text: A pancake is flat, but a ball is round.
A table has a flat top.

tiny.text: An ant is tiny next to an elephant.

huge.text: Blue whales are huge; they are the biggest animals ever.

large.text: Large is another word for big.
A pizza can be small, medium, or large.

small.text: A mouse is small, and an elephant is big.
Small is the opposite of large.

thick.text: A tree trunk is thick, but a twig is thin.
A thick book has lots of pages.

narrow.text: A narrow path has room for only one person.
Narrow is the opposite of wide.

shallow.text: Little kids swim in the shallow end of a pool.
Shallow is the opposite of deep.

heavy.text: An elephant is heavy, and a feather is light.
A bowling ball is heavier than a balloon.

light.text: A feather is light, so the wind can blow it away.
Light also means bright, like the sun.

taller.text: A giraffe is taller than a horse.
You get taller as you grow.

biggest.text: The blue whale is the biggest animal of all.
Of a mouse, a dog, and a horse, the horse is the biggest.

smallest.text: Of a cat, a mouse, and a cow, the mouse is the smallest.
Your little finger is your smallest finger.

same.text: Two plus two and three plus one are the same.

different.text: A cat and a dog are different animals.
Apples and bananas are different, but both are fruit.

more.text: More is the opposite of less.

less.text: A cup holds less water than a bucket.

fewer.text: A bird has fewer legs than a dog.

most.text: Of two, five, and nine cookies, nine is the most.
Most is the opposite of least.

least.text: Of four, one, and six, one is the least.

zero.text: Three take away three is zero.

few.text: A few means a small number, like two or three.
There are only a few cookies left.

none.text: If you eat all the grapes, there are none left.

both.text: Both of your hands have five fingers.
Cats and dogs both have fur.

several.text: Several means more than two, but not many.
An octopus has several arms: eight in all.

pair.text: A pair is two things that go together.
You wear a pair of shoes.

double.text: Double means two times as many.

dozen.text: Eggs often come in a box of a dozen.

equal.text: Two plus two is equal to four.

empty.text: An empty box has nothing in it.
Empty is the opposite of full.

full.text: A full glass has no room for more.
The moon looks round and bright when it is full.

whole.text: You ate the whole apple, so none is left.
A whole is all of something.

extra.text: Extra means more than you need.
Bring an extra sock in case one gets wet.

plenty.text: There is plenty of food for everyone.

under.text: The cat is hiding under the bed.
Under is the opposite of over.

over.text: A bird flies over the house.

above.text: The sky is above the ground.

below.text: Below is the opposite of above.

behind.text: The moon hid behind a cloud.

beside.text: The spoon goes beside the bowl.

between.text: Your nose is between your eyes.
Five comes between four and six.

inside.text: A turtle can pull its head inside its shell.
Inside is the opposite of outside.

outside.text: We play outside when it is sunny.
The bark is on the outside of a tree.

around.text: The Earth goes around the sun.
A fence goes all the way around the yard.

across.text: A bridge goes across a river.
You walk across the street at a crosswalk.

middle.text: Your nose is in the middle of your face.
Two is the middle number of one, two, three.

front.text: Your face is on the front of your head.
Front is the opposite of back.

bottom.text: Roots are at the bottom of a plant.
Bottom is the opposite of top.

left.text: Most people write with their right hand, not their left.
Left is the opposite of right.

right.text: Right is the opposite of left.

near.text: Near is the opposite of far.

far.text: The stars are very far away.
The moon is farther away than the clouds.

corner.text: Two walls meet at a corner.

first.text: An egg comes first, then a chick.
The first letter of the alphabet is A.

last.text: Z is the last letter of the alphabet.
Last is the opposite of first.

next.text: After Monday, the next day is Tuesday.

before.text: You put on socks before shoes.

after.text: After is the opposite of before.

begin.text: Every race has a place to begin and a place to end.

finish.text: The first runner to finish wins the race.

early.text: Early is the opposite of late.
The sun comes up early in the morning.

late.text: Owls stay up late at night.
If you are late, you missed the start.

soon.text: Soon means in a short time.
It is dark, so it will soon be bedtime.

today.text: Today is the day it is now.

tonight.text: You might see the moon tonight if the sky is clear.

morning.text: The sun rises in the morning.

noon.text: Noon is the middle of the day.
At noon, the sun is high in the sky.

week.text: Monday is a day of the week.

spring.text: In spring, flowers start to grow.
A spring is also a coil that bounces back.

season.text: Spring, summer, fall, and winter are the four seasons.
Each season lasts about three months.

yesterday.text: Yesterday was the day before today.
Tomorrow comes after today, and yesterday came before it.

circle.text: A circle is round and has no corners.
A wheel is shaped like a circle.

square.text: A square has four sides that are all the same length.
A square is a kind of rectangle.

triangle.text: A triangle has three sides and three corners.
A slice of pizza looks like a triangle.

oval.text: An egg is shaped like an oval.
An oval is like a stretched circle.

diamond.text: A kite is often shaped like a diamond.
A diamond is also a very hard, shiny stone.

cone.text: A party hat is shaped like a cone.
A cone is round at the bottom and pointy at the top.

sphere.text: The Earth is shaped like a sphere.

line.text: A straight line goes from one point to another.
You wait in line for your turn.

curve.text: A curve is a line that bends.
The letter C is a curve.

angle.text: An angle is made where two lines meet.
A square has four angles that are all the same.

stripe.text: A zebra has black and white stripes.
A stripe is a long, thin band of color.

spiral.text: A snail's shell has a spiral shape.
A spiral goes around and around, getting bigger.

pattern.text: Red, blue, red, blue is a pattern.
A pattern repeats again and again.

row.text: Chairs can stand in a row, side by side.
To row a boat, you pull the oars.

shape.text: A circle, a square, and a triangle are all shapes.
A shape is the outline of something.

edge.text: An edge is where something ends.

dot.text: A dot is a tiny round mark.
A period at the end of a sentence is a dot.

point.text: A pencil has a sharp point.
To point, you use your finger.

center.text: The center is the middle of something.
A bullseye is the center of a target.

smooth.text: Smooth is the opposite of rough.

soft.text: Soft is the opposite of hard.

hard.text: Hard can also mean not easy.

sharp.text: A knife is sharp, so be careful.
Sharp is the opposite of dull.

sticky.text: Tape is sticky on one side.

shiny.text: Metal can be shiny when it is clean.

bumpy.text: A road with holes is bumpy.

metal.text: A spoon can be made of metal.

wood.text: Tables can be made of wood.

glass.text: You can see through clear glass.

plastic.text: Many toys are made of plastic.
A water bottle can be made of plastic.

happy.text: You smile when you are happy.
Happy is the opposite of sad.

angry.text: When you feel angry, take a deep breath.

proud.text: You feel proud when you do something well.
The team was proud of its win.

calm.text: A lake is calm when there is no wind.

brave.text: Brave means not giving up when you are scared.

scared.text: Loud thunder can make you feel scared.

tired.text: You feel tired after running a long way.
When you are tired, you need sleep.

animal.text: A dog, a fish, and a bird are all animals.
An animal is a living thing that can move on its own.

mammal.text: A whale is a mammal, not a fish.
A mammal has hair or fur and feeds its babies milk.

reptile.text: Snakes, lizards, and turtles are reptiles.
A reptile has dry, scaly skin.

insect.text: A spider is not an insect; it has eight legs.

bird.text: A bird has feathers and wings.
A penguin is a bird that cannot fly.

vehicle.text: A car, a bus, and a train are all vehicles.
A vehicle carries people or things from place to place.

tool.text: A hammer is a tool for hitting nails.
A tool helps you do a job.

fruit.text: Apples, bananas, and grapes are all fruits.
A fruit holds the seeds of a plant.

vegetable.text: A carrot is a vegetable that grows under the ground.

plant.text: A plant needs water and sunlight to grow.
Trees, grass, and flowers are all plants.

furniture.text: Chairs, beds, and tables are furniture.
A sofa is a piece of furniture.

clothing.text: Shirts, socks, and hats are all clothing.

instrument.text: A drum and a violin are both instruments.
You play music on an instrument.

weather.text: Rain, snow, and wind are kinds of weather.
The weather is what the sky is doing outside.

planet.text: Earth is the planet we live on.
Our sun has eight planets going around it.

body.text: Your body has two arms and two legs.
Your heart pumps blood around your body.

family.text: Parents, brothers, and sisters are part of a family.
A family is people who belong together.

food.text: Bread, cheese, and apples are all food.

drink.text: Milk, juice, and water are things you drink.
Plants drink water through their roots.

place.text: A park, a school, and a store are all places.
Put your toys back in their place.

forest.text: A forest is a place with lots of trees.
Deer and owls live in the forest.

desert.text: A desert gets very little rain.
Camels can live in the desert.

ocean.text: The ocean is huge and full of salty water.
Whales and sharks live in the ocean.

island.text: An island is land with water all around it.

river.text: A river is water that flows downhill.

mountain.text: A mountain is much taller than a hill.
Snow can stay on top of a mountain all year.

volcano.text: Hot melted rock comes out of a volcano.
A volcano can make a new island.

jungle.text: A jungle is hot, wet, and full of plants.
Monkeys and parrots live in the jungle.

pond.text: A pond is smaller than a lake.
Frogs and ducks live near a pond.

cave.text: A cave is a hole in a hill or rock.

tadpole.text: A tadpole grows into a frog.
A tadpole lives in water and has a tail.

caterpillar.text: A caterpillar can turn into a butterfly.
A caterpillar eats lots of leaves.

cocoon.text: A moth grows inside a cocoon.
A cocoon is a soft case made of silk.

butterfly.text: A butterfly starts life as a caterpillar.

sprout.text: A sprout is a new plant that has just come up.
A seed can sprout when it gets water.

blossom.text: A blossom is a flower on a tree.

shadow.text: Your shadow is dark where you block the light.
Your shadow gets long when the sun is low.

thunder.text: Thunder is the loud boom in a storm.
You see lightning before you hear thunder.

rainbow.text: A rainbow can appear when the sun shines through rain.

magnet.text: A magnet pulls on things made of iron.
Magnetic cubes stick together because of magnets.

calf.text: A baby cow is called a calf.
A baby whale is also called a calf.

foal.text: A baby horse is called a foal.
Cow is to calf as horse is to foal.

cub.text: A baby bear is called a cub.
Baby lions are called cubs too.

lamb.text: A baby sheep is called a lamb.
Dog is to puppy as sheep is to lamb.

chick.text: A baby chicken is called a chick.
A chick hatches from an egg.

kitten.text: A baby cat is called a kitten.
A kitten grows up to be a cat.

hive.text: Bird is to nest as bee is to hive.

den.text: A fox lives in a den.
Bears can sleep all winter in a den.

burrow.text: A rabbit lives in a burrow under the ground.
A burrow is a hole an animal digs to live in.

barn.text: Cows and horses can sleep in a barn.
A farmer keeps hay in a barn.

kennel.text: A dog can sleep in a kennel.
Bird is to nest as dog is to kennel.

stable.text: Stable also means steady and not wobbly.

farmer.text: A farmer grows food and raises animals.

baker.text: A baker makes bread and cakes.

doctor.text: A doctor helps sick people get well.
A doctor listens to your heart.

pilot.text: Driver is to car as pilot is to plane.

builder.text: A builder uses a hammer and nails.

dentist.text: A dentist takes care of your teeth.
You visit the dentist to keep your teeth healthy.

nurse.text: A nurse helps sick people in a hospital.
A nurse and a doctor work together.

painter.text: A painter uses a brush and paint.
A painter can paint a picture or a wall.

bark.text: Bark is also the rough skin of a tree.

trunk.text: An elephant's nose is called a trunk.
A tree trunk holds up its branches.

bank.text: You keep money in a bank.
The side of a river is called a bank.

match.text: A match can light a fire.
Socks that match look the same.

seal.text: A seal is an animal that swims in the sea.
To seal an envelope is to close it tight.

watch.text: A watch tells the time on your wrist.
To watch means to look at something.

bill.text: A duck's mouth is called a bill.
A bill is also paper money.

club.text: A club is a group of people who meet.
A golf club is a stick for hitting a ball.

palm.text: The palm is the inside of your hand.
A palm tree has big leaves at the top.

crane.text: A crane is a bird with long legs.
A crane is also a machine that lifts heavy things.

mouse.text: A mouse is a small animal with a long tail.
A computer mouse helps you point and click.

glasses.text: Some people wear glasses to see better.

pitcher.text: A pitcher holds water or juice for pouring.
In baseball, the pitcher throws the ball.

block.text: A block is a toy you can stack.
A city block has streets on all four sides.

key.text: A piano has black and white keys.

nail.text: You hit a nail with a hammer.
Your fingers have nails at the tips.

pupil.text: A pupil is a student in a school.
The pupil is the black circle in your eye.

letter.text: A is the first letter of the alphabet.
You can mail a letter to a friend.

ruler.text: A ruler measures how long things are.
A king or queen is a ruler.

fly.text: A fly is a small insect with wings.
